transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

I don't know. I guess... I just don't feel like myself anymore. 

I stopped doing things. Hiking, coaching... playing my guitar. I don't really call people back either. Mostly I just sit in my rental for hours. I know there's stuff I need to do, but I just... can't make myself start. That's about it.
About how long have you been feeling this way?
A while. I guess... maybe a year and two months. It was around the time I moved into this smaller rental... after my divorce. Things just sort of unraveled since then.
{"intent": "Screen for a history of manic or hypomanic episodes to evaluate for bipolar disorder.", "question": "Have you ever had times in your life where you felt the opposite—
No. I don't think so. Just... what I told you.
Before your divorce, had you ever gone through a period where you felt this down or lost interest in things?
No. I don't think so. I was... fine, mostly. It just started after.
How has your sleep been during this past year?
I don't really know. It's... fine, I guess. I just sleep when I can. I don't really pay attention to it.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight over this past year?
No. Not really. I eat the same, I think. Weight's probably the same.
How have your energy levels been over this past year?
I don't know. About the same, I guess. I just... get through the day. I haven't really noticed anything different.
Have you been feeling down on yourself, worthless, or having strong feelings of guilt?
No. I don't really... think about that kind of stuff. I just go about my day. So, no. Nothing like that.
Have you had any thoughts that life isn't worth living, or thoughts of hurting yourself?
No. I don't... I don't have thoughts like that. No.
Have you found it harder to concentrate, focus on things, or make everyday decisions?
Not really. I just... do what I need to do. Decisions are just... regular things. I haven't noticed any trouble.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient developed depressed mood, loss of interest in previously enjoyed activities, and social withdrawal following a major life stressor (divorce and relocation). The symptoms have persisted for approximately 14 months, which fits ICD-10 criteria for a prolonged depressive reaction (F43.21). Criteria for a major depressive episode are not met as neurovegetative and cognitive symptoms (sleep, appetite, energy, guilt, suicidal ideation, concentration) are absent.
